title: Locked checks and weakened tests
bridge: A locked check is like a Playwright test in CI that your PR must pass. Except here the agent cannot edit the test it is judged by: GitHub refuses the merge, whatever the prompt says.
intro: An agent can make CI green by weakening the thing that judges it. This lesson builds two checks in RhinoHealth/ai-agents. One blocks agent PRs that edit CI, lint or test settings. The other warns a reviewer when a test got easier to pass.

picture.caption: Two jobs run on every fcp PR. locked-checks fails an agent PR that touches a locked path; weakened-tests marks risky test edits for the reviewer.

steps.text: opens a PR; the diff touches frontend/vitest.config.js and a test file
gives the job the list of locked paths for fcp
the job lists the changed files and matches them against the list
a match: the required check fails and names the file; the ruleset blocks the merge
the job reads each file's patch and counts removed assertions, new skips, changed thresholds
one ::warning annotation per finding on the diff; the reviewer decides

sections.h: A PR that lowers the bar
p: Picture an agent PR in RhinoHealth/fcp. The ticket asked for a bug fix in cloud/, and the diff also touches cloud/.coveragerc and lowers fail-under. CI goes green. Nobody asked for that change.
A required check is a CI job that a PR must pass before GitHub allows the merge. The fcp ruleset from lesson g0-1 lists them by name. This lesson adds two more jobs to that list.
The first, locked checks, fails an agent PR that edits the files that judge it. The second, weakened tests, marks test edits that make a test easier to pass. One blocks, the other warns.

sections.h: Two walls, one list of paths
p: The first wall already exists from lesson g0-2. The rhino-ai-agents GitHub App has no workflows permission. GitHub refuses any push from it that touches .github/workflows, before any check runs.

The second wall is this check. Its list of locked paths lives in ai-agents/settings/protected-paths.yaml, one block per repo. The harness hooks in G3-21 read the same file inside the VM, so the hook and the check never disagree.
A wall is a rule that infrastructure enforces, not a prompt. Here GitHub enforces it: the check is required in the ruleset, and the agent has no way to change it.

callout.text: Agents never change the checks they are judged by. The check that enforces this lives in RhinoHealth/ai-agents, a repo the agent's one-repo token never covers.

p: The file sits in ai-agents/checks/src/ next to independent-approval.ts from lesson g0-3. The whole sketch is 33 lines, so we read it in two parts. This part holds the imports, the locked paths and the two types.

A glob is a path pattern: .github/** means every file under .github at any depth. Node's node:path has matchesGlob, which tests one path against one pattern. Check the docs for node:path matchesGlob if Node prints an experimental warning.
Only the file-path comment line is dropped from the sketch; the blank line between the two parts is the split point.
sections.because: We keep the locked list in readable code, because the reviewer who adds a path must see the whole rule.

notes.text: The comment states the rule: agent PRs are limited, human PRs are not.
matchesGlob from node:path tests one file path against one glob pattern.
isDeepStrictEqual from node:util compares two parsed objects field by field, so key order does not matter.
smol-toml parses TOML text into an object. We compare parsed sections, so a comment or a blank line never counts as a change.
Only PRs opened by this bot login are limited. Every other author passes at once.
fcp's block of settings/protected-paths.yaml, copied inline here so you can read it. The real code loads the file.
Every file under .github: workflows, scripts and the PR template.
The verify entry points from G7. An agent must not edit the script that proves its own work.
Backend lint settings: flake8 and the pre-commit hooks.
Frontend lint, type and unit-test settings, including vitest coverage thresholds.
Playwright and Stryker settings: retries, timeouts and mutation thresholds.
Coverage settings for cloud, client and sdk, and sdk's tox.ini.
Only these [tool.*] sections of pyproject.toml are locked. The dependencies in that file may still change.
A regular expression that finds the HTML comment block the orchestrator writes into the PR body in G4.
A function type: give it a path and a commit sha, get the file text. main() builds it with Octokit, the GitHub client from lesson p2-5.
The parts of the PR we need: author login, body, and the base and head commit shas.

p: This part is the function the job calls. It returns a list of strings. An empty list means the PR passes.

pyproject.toml is a special case. Agents may change dependencies in it, because an upgrade routine will do that. They may not change [tool.black], [tool.isort], [tool.flake8], [tool.coverage] or [tool.pytest].
So the function reads the file at the base commit and at the head commit, parses both, and compares only those sections. A text diff would also flag a moved dependency line, which is allowed.
sections.because: We compare parsed sections rather than text, because the rule is about settings, not about lines.

notes.text: Inputs: the PR, the changed file paths, and the readFile function. Passing readFile in lets a test fake GitHub.
A human PR returns an empty list before anything else runs.
Pull the plan's locked block out of the PR body. ?.[1] is the captured text, or undefined when there is no block.
The locked list is the static list plus the plan's file list, split on whitespace, with empty strings removed.
A changed file is bad when any locked pattern matches it.
The pyproject.toml special case only runs when the PR touched that file.
tool(sha) reads pyproject.toml at one commit, parses it, and returns its tool table, or an empty object.
Both versions are read in parallel with Promise.all.
Each locked section that differs becomes one entry, for example pyproject.toml [tool.black].
A non-empty list fails the job and lists each file. A person can then take the PR over.

sections.h: Run it as a job in fcp
p: The check runs the way lesson g0-3 runs independent-approval. fcp's caller workflow gets a second job that runs node /app/dist/locked-checks.js in the same ai-agents-checks image. The image is pinned by digest, and fcp never checks out the private ai-agents repo.

main() in the file uses Octokit to list the PR's changed files and to read pyproject.toml at both commits. It calls violations, prints each entry, and sets process.exitCode = 1 when the list is not empty.
Then ask DevOps to add the job's exact name to the fcp ruleset's required checks. Eval sets need no entry: they live in the restricted golden-set repo, which the agent's one-repo token never covers.

callout.text: Until G4 writes the <!-- ai-agents:locked-checks --> block into the PR body, only the static list applies. The code above already handles both.

sections.h: Weakened tests: warn, do not block
p: Tests change with the code, so an agent may edit existing tests. But the one reviewer must see when an edit makes a test easier to pass. That is G0-19: a check on every PR, from people and agents, that annotates and never fails.
It reads each changed file's patch. A patch is the unified diff GitHub returns per file: lines starting with + were added, lines starting with - were removed. The check only looks at those lines.

It counts removed and added assertions in test files, flags new skips or .only, and flags removed lines that held a threshold. The sketch is 27 lines; we dropped the file-path comment and two blank lines, nothing else.
sections.because: We read the patch rather than the whole file, because the question is what this PR changed.

notes.text: Annotations only. Editing tests is allowed; the reviewer gets a pointer, not a red check.
Which paths count as test files: tests/, e2e/, integration-tests/, *.test.ts(x), *.spec.ts(x) and Python test_*.py.
Lines that assert something, in vitest, Playwright, node:assert and pytest style.
A new it.skip, test.only, xit or @pytest.mark.skip means a test stopped running, or every other test did.
A number next to fail-under, thresholds, retries or timeout. The check cannot know the direction, so it asks the reviewer to look.
A finding is a pair: the kind and the line text.
One call per changed file, with its path and its patch.
The first character is the diff sign; the rest is the line as written.
Skip context lines, and the +++ and --- file headers that also start with those signs.
Assertion lines are counted only in test files, removed and added separately.
An added skip or focus is a finding on its own.
A removed threshold line is a finding that asks: check it was not loosened.
Only a net loss of assertions is reported, so a rewritten assertion counts as zero.
main() prints each finding as a ::warning file=<path>:: line and writes a job summary.

p: The job prints one ::warning file=<path>:: line per finding. GitHub turns these into annotations on the diff, with no PR comment and no write permission. A short job summary lists the same findings.
The job also writes the findings as JSON in its output, so G4's scope judge and the PR story can quote them.

Before you turn it on, run it over the last 50 merged fcp PRs. The target is at most one false alarm per ten PRs. A false alarm is a warning on a change that weakened nothing; a pattern that makes more than that is dropped.

Both functions take plain values, so node:test can drive them without GitHub, as in lesson p1-6. For violations you pass a fake readFile that returns two pyproject.toml strings. For findings you pass a small patch string.
The third test shows the order of findings: the skip is pushed inside the loop, the assertion count after it.
sections.because: We fake readFile instead of calling GitHub, because the test must run offline and finish in a second.

notes.text: With tsx, importing ../src/locked-checks.js resolves to the .ts file next to it.
The base commit's pyproject.toml: black at 120 columns and one dependency.
The head commit changes only the dependency version. That is allowed.
The fake readFile: it ignores the path and picks a string by sha.
A PR by the agent bot; the shas are the words the fake understands.
Same files, human author: an empty list.
The workflow file is reported; pyproject.toml is not, because [tool.black] is equal on both sides.
A three-line patch: one expect removed, one it.skip added, one context line.
The skip finding comes first, with the trimmed line text.
One assertion removed and none added: a net loss of one.

quiz.q: An agent PR changes pyproject.toml. What does locked-checks do with it?

options.text: Fails the PR, because pyproject.toml is on the locked list.
options.why: It is not on the list. Agents may change dependencies there, so the whole file is not locked.

options.text: Parses the file at base and head and compares only the [tool.black], [tool.isort], [tool.flake8], [tool.coverage] and [tool.pytest] sections.
options.why: That is the partial lock: settings are compared as parsed objects, dependencies may change.

options.text: Ignores it, because dependency upgrades are allowed.
options.why: Dependencies may change, but a lowered coverage fail-under in the same file must still fail the PR.

options.text: Every PR in fcp, from people and agents.
options.why: People may edit CI and lint settings; violations returns an empty list for a human author at once.

options.text: Only PRs whose body has an ai-agents:locked-checks block.
options.why: The block adds files from the plan; the static list applies to every agent PR even without it.
AGENT_BOTS holds that login; agents never change the checks they are judged by, people may.

quiz.q: weakened-tests finds a new it.only in a PR. What happens?

options.text: A ::warning annotation appears on that line of the diff and the reviewer decides.
options.why: The check annotates and never fails: editing tests is allowed, the reviewer must see it.

options.text: The required check fails and the merge is blocked until the .only is removed.
options.why: That is what locked-checks does for locked paths. weakened-tests does not block.

options.text: The bot posts a PR comment listing the finding.
options.why: No PR comment is written, so the job needs no write permission.

words.plain: A CI job named in the ruleset that a PR must pass before GitHub allows the merge.
A required check that fails an agent PR when it edits the files that judge it.
A path pattern such as .github/**, where ** matches any depth of folders.
The unified diff for one file: + lines were added, - lines were removed, the rest is context.
A note GitHub shows on a line of the diff, created by printing a ::warning file=<path>:: line in a job.
A warning on a change that weakened nothing; more than one per ten PRs means the pattern is dropped.

tickets.why: This lesson showed the locked list, the pyproject.toml partial lock, and how the job runs in fcp's caller.
walk: Confirm the first wall: the rhino-ai-agents App from G0-08 has no workflows permission, so GitHub refuses its pushes to .github/workflows.
Add ai-agents/checks/src/locked-checks.ts (the two blocks above) next to independent-approval.ts, and put fcp's list in ai-agents/settings/protected-paths.yaml, one block per repo.
Keep pyproject.toml partly locked: parse both versions with smol-toml and compare [tool.black], [tool.isort], [tool.flake8], [tool.coverage] and [tool.pytest] with isDeepStrictEqual.
Read the plan's file list from the <!-- ai-agents:locked-checks --> block in the PR body. Until G4 writes it, only the static list applies.
Add a second job to fcp's caller workflow: node /app/dist/locked-checks.js in the same ai-agents-checks image. Human PRs pass straight through.
With DevOps, add the job's exact name to the fcp ruleset's required checks. Eval sets need no entry: they live in the restricted golden-set repo.
Lock fcp's verify entry points too: .claude/settings.json with its Stop hook, scripts/claude_stop_verify.sh, scripts/poe_verify.py and frontend/scripts/verify.ts from G7.

tickets.why: This lesson showed how findings() reads a patch and why the job annotates instead of failing.
walk: Add ai-agents/checks/src/weakened-tests.ts (the block above). Run it as a third job in fcp's caller, node /app/dist/weakened-tests.js, on every PR from people and agents.

Cover fcp's test files: frontend/test/unit/**, frontend/e2e/**, **/tests/** and cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/integration-tests/**; thresholds are coverage fail-under, vitest coverage thresholds, Playwright retries and timeouts.
Print one ::warning annotation per finding on its file plus a short job summary. No PR comment, so no write permission is needed.
Calibrate on the last 50 merged fcp PRs: at most one false alarm per ten PRs, or drop the noisy pattern.
Write the findings as JSON in the job output, so G4's scope judge and the PR story can quote them.

remember: Agents never change the checks they are judged by: locked-checks blocks the edit, weakened-tests shows the reviewer what got easier.
